records.headline: FAA AD 2026-12-06 (effective June 30, 2026): Trent 1000 HPT blade failure risk — Trent family read-across

records.root_cause: Premature failure of high-pressure turbine (HPT) blades despite existing inspection and life-limit requirements.

records.headline: EASA Emergency AD 2026-0119-E: A380 wing mid-spar crack inspections (Emirates/Qantas) — effective June 24, 2026

records.headline: NTSB preliminary report (DCA26FA194): United 767-400 (Flight 169) struck light pole on approach to Newark
records.summary: United Airlines Flight 169, a Boeing 767-400ER (N77066) from Venice to Newark, struck a light pole over the New Jersey Turnpike on approach to runway 29 on 3 May 2026 (debris hit a tractor-trailer, minor injury to the driver); the aircraft sustained substantial fuselage damage. NTSB released a preliminary report on 4 June 2026 under docket DCA26FA194, finding the aircraft was below the normal glidepath, with the first officer warning the captain the aircraft was 'slow' and 'a little low' shortly before impact.
records.root_cause: Reported (trade press characterization of NTSB preliminary findings): aircraft remained below normal glide path for the final approach segment; first officer warned the captain the aircraft was slow and low shortly before impact.
records.read_across: 767 is a Boeing widebody peer type; approach-energy-management and CRM lessons are relevant to 777 line operations even though airframe-specific systems differ.
records.verifier_notes: Corrected docket number from scanner's erroneous DCA26MA024 to DCA26FA194. PDF binary fetched but text unextractable; held at UNVERIFIED per verbatim-excerpt rule.

records.headline: JAL A350-1000 diverts to Keflavik over right-engine oil system malfunction (Trent XWB-97), June 14 2026
records.summary: A Japan Airlines Airbus A350-1000 (JA02WJ), operating flight JL43 Tokyo Haneda-London Heathrow with 222 passengers and 17 crew, diverted to Keflavik, Iceland on 14 June 2026 after the crew identified a right-hand engine oil system malfunction while over Greenland at FL370, landing safely on runway 01. The aircraft is powered by Trent XWB-97, the same engine variant used on CX's own A350-1000 fleet. No associated AD/SB has surfaced.
records.read_across: Same aircraft type and engine variant (A350-1000 / Trent XWB-97) operated by Cathay Pacific; an oil-system malfunction on this engine type warrants monitoring for any related OEM bulletin.
records.verifier_notes: Event confirmed via The Aviation Herald (tier 4, leads-only) — no primary regulator/OEM document exists; rolled up as REPORTED.

records.headline: FAA AD 2025-25-12: A350 flight-control software update closes out FCRM hydraulic-fluid contamination risk (effective Jan 13, 2026)
records.summary: FAA AD 2025-25-12 (Amendment 39-23220, docket FAA-2025-5390), published 29 December 2025 and effective 13 January 2026, requires Airbus A350-941/-1041 operators to install Flight Control and Guidance System software standards PRIM P14.1.3 and SEC S14.1.2, permanently closing out a risk of loss of control of an outboard aileron (and, by shared design, elevator/rudder) surfaces caused by hydraulic fluid contaminating an electronic card in the Flight Control Remote Module. It supersedes interim AD 2025-13-12 (July 2025).

references.effectivity: Airbus SAS Model A350-941 and A350-1041 airplanes
references.fetched_text_snippet: Loss of control of an outboard aileron surface due to hydraulic fluid contaminating an electronic card of the flight control remote module.

audit.excerpt: This AD was prompted by a report of loss of control of an outboard aileron surface due to hydraulic fluid contaminating an electronic card of the flight control remote module (FCRM).
audit.notes: AD 2025-25-12 and effectivity (A350-941/-1041) confirmed. Cited quote is an exact substring of the actual sentence.

records.oem_regulator_position: Software fix is positioned as the permanent mitigation, replacing the interim hardware-replacement program required by superseded AD 2025-13-12.
records.root_cause: Hydraulic fluid contaminated an electronic card of the Flight Control Remote Module (FCRM), which could cause loss of control of an outboard aileron surface.

quotes.text: Loss of control of an outboard aileron surface due to hydraulic fluid contaminating an electronic card of the flight control remote module.

records.verifier_notes: Confirmed via govinfo.gov. Developing carryover: permanent software fix superseding recent interim AD; directly affects both CX A350 subtypes.

records.headline: FAA AD 2025-25-07: GE90 HPT stage 1/2 disk replacement for iron-inclusion powder-metal defect (effective Feb 6, 2026)
records.summary: FAA AD 2025-25-07 (docket FAA-2025-1364), published 2 January 2026 and effective 6 February 2026, requires replacement of GE90-90B/-94B/-110B1/-115B HPT stage 1 and stage 2 disks identified in AD Table 1 or referenced GE service-bulletin tables, due to a manufacturing process that may have introduced iron inclusion into the powder-metal material, risking premature fracture and uncontained failure. GE90-115B powers the CX 777-300ER fleet.

references.effectivity: General Electric GE90-90B, GE90-94B, GE90-110B1, and GE90-115B turbofan engines with specific HPT stage 1/2 disks identified by part/serial number
references.fetched_text_snippet: The FAA is issuing this AD to prevent premature fracture and uncontained failure of the HPT stage 1 disks and HPT stage 2 disks.

audit.excerpt: This AD was prompted by a manufacturer investigation that revealed certain HPT stage 1 disks and HPT stage 2 disks were manufactured from powder metal material suspected to contain iron inclusion. The FAA is issuing this AD to prevent premature fracture and uncontained failure of the HPT stage 1 disks and HPT stage 2 disks.
audit.notes: AD 2025-25-07 and engine models GE90-90B/-94B/-110B1/-115B confirmed. Quoted text confirmed verbatim.

records.root_cause: HPT stage 1/2 disks manufactured from powder metal material suspected to contain iron inclusion, reducing fatigue life and raising risk of premature fracture / uncontained failure.

quotes.text: The FAA is issuing this AD to prevent premature fracture and uncontained failure of the HPT stage 1 disks and HPT stage 2 disks.
quotes.doc_title: Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines

records.verifier_notes: Confirmed via govinfo.gov. Outside window but directly fleet-relevant compliance item (GE90-115B is the CX 777-300ER engine).

records.headline: FAA AD 2025-24-51 / EASA AD 2025-0268-E: A320-family ELAC software fix for solar-radiation pitch event (effective Jan 6, 2026)
records.summary: Following an Airbus A320 uncommanded, limited pitch-down event attributed to intense solar radiation corrupting an Elevator Aileron Computer (ELAC), EASA issued emergency AD 2025-0268-E (effective 29 Nov 2025) and the FAA mirrored it with emergency AD 2025-24-51 (Amendment 39-23223, docket FAA-2025-5395), published 5 January 2026 and effective 6 January 2026, both requiring replacement/modification of affected ELACs. The FAA AD's effectivity list explicitly includes A321-251NX/-252NX/-253NX/-271NX/-272NX — the CX A321neo configuration family.

records.headline: FAA AD 2025-26-04: PW1122G-JM through PW1431GH-JM fuel hose clamp / fan blade fire risk (effective Feb 17, 2026) — read-across
records.summary: FAA AD 2025-26-04 (Amendment 39-23226, docket FAA-2025-0480), published 12 January 2026 and effective 17 February 2026, addresses Pratt & Whitney geared-turbofan engines (PW1122G-JM through PW1431GH-JM model range, encompassing the PW1100G-JM/PW1400G-JM families) after multiple reports of fan blade fracture events, three resulting in an engine under-cowl or pool fire. Requires removal of a loop cushion clamp (P/N ST1540-06) within 30 days and replacement of thermal management system clevis mounts at next shop visit. CX's own A321neo fleet uses LEAP-1A, not PW1100G, so this is read-across only.

records.headline: NTSB UPS MD-11 (Flight 2976, docket DCA26MA024) investigative hearing — May 19-20, 2026: aft-pylon bearing fatigue findings
records.summary: NTSB held a two-day investigative hearing (19-20 May 2026, docket DCA26MA024, confirmed on ntsb.gov) into the 4 November 2025 crash of UPS Flight 2976, an MD-11F that lost its No.1 engine/pylon on takeoff from Louisville, killing 3 crew and 11 on the ground. Trade press reporting on the hearing describes fatigue cracking in an aft pylon spherical bearing (P/N S00399-1), prior bearing-failure incidents referenced in a 2011 Boeing service letter (MD-11-SL-54-104-A), and Boeing testimony that the bearing should have been classified as a Principal Structural Element at original certification. The FAA's emergency AD grounded MD-11/DC-10/MD-10 variants in November 2025; that grounding was eased in May 2026 per trade press.

references.fetched_text_snippet: The three crewmembers aboard the airplane were killed. Eleven people on the ground were killed and another 23 injured.

audit.excerpt: last year's crash of a United Parcel Service MD-11F cargo airplane shortly after takeoff from Louisville, Kentucky. The three crewmembers aboard the airplane were killed. Eleven people on the ground were killed and another 23 injured.
audit.notes: Docket DCA26MA024 referenced multiple times; hearing dates May 19-20, 2026 confirmed; casualty text confirmed verbatim.

records.oem_regulator_position: Reported (trade press characterization of hearing testimony): Boeing staff acknowledged the failed aft pylon spherical bearing should have been classified as a Principal Structural Element during original MD-11 certification.
records.root_cause: Reported (trade press characterization): fatigue cracking in the bearing race propagated until overstress fracture of both lugs, shifting load and allowing engine/pylon separation.

quotes.text: The three crewmembers aboard the airplane were killed. Eleven people on the ground were killed and another 23 injured.
quotes.doc_title: Investigative Hearing: UPS Flight 2976 Crash During Takeoff

records.read_across: Classic major industry event — pylon/engine-mount structural integrity and the OEM-service-letter-vs-mandatory-AD gap is a read-across theme for all CX fleet types, even though CX operates no MD-11/DC-10.
records.verifier_notes: Hearing dates/docket confirmed directly on ntsb.gov with genuine excerpt. FAA emergency AD reference remains UNVERIFIED (not independently fetched). Hearing just outside window; carried over as the canonical major industry event.
